name: io.github.emmanuelorta/crawlcheck
title: CrawlCheck
description: Verification layer for the agentic web: a signed answer about any site before an agent acts.

tools.name: preflight
tools.description: Returns one signed go/no-go decision (allow, warn, require_confirmation, block or unsupported) for one action on one domain: read, cite, connect, transact or administer. Use it before acting on a site you have not checked. Pass agent (your crawler token) to have robots.txt checked. For the evidence behind the decision use resolve_domain; to choose between several sites use best_source.

action.description: What you are about to do (default read)

agent.description: Your crawler user-agent token, e.g. GPTBot

template.description: safe_citation, safe_data_retrieval, safe_api_connect, safe_mcp_tool, safe_commerce, safe_oauth or support_escalation

policy.description: max_age_hours, on_warn (warn|require_confirmation|block), require_entity, human_approval[], allow[], deny[]

tools.name: best_source
tools.description: Ranks 2 to 10 candidate sites, or the measured businesses for a trade and city, by what CrawlCheck verified, with signed reasons for and against each. Sites that share a phone number or homepage text are grouped as one network. Use when choosing which business or site to cite, recommend or call. For one site you already chose use preflight.

domains.description: Candidate sites, bare domains, up to 10

tools.name: resolve_domain
tools.description: Returns the full signed record for one domain: what it claims, what each crawler is actually served, who controls it, a decision per action, what changed, and the evidence and time behind each part. A domain never measured gets a partial answer naming what was not read. For one go/no-go decision use preflight; for a fresh graded scan use scan_domain.

tools.name: field_check
tools.description: Returns a signed verdict on one business fact you hold (phone, address, hours or service area), checked against the business's own site and its dated history. Verdicts include matches, former_value, not_this_business and not_published. Use before repeating or acting on a business's contact details. For the whole record about the domain use resolve_domain.

domain.description: Bare domain of the business, e.g. example.com

value.description: The value you hold: a 10-digit number, a street address, a week (Mo-Fr 08:00-17:00) or a moment (Sa 10:00), or a place name

tools.name: scan_domain
tools.description: Scans a domain now (5-15 seconds) and returns its graded record: grade, score, section scores and findings. CrawlCheck's scanner sends other crawlers' user-agent strings, so site logs show those names; they are not visits by those crawlers. A domain scanned in the last 2 minutes returns that report, marked reused: true with its scanned_at. A null grade means not measured, not low.

domain.description: A bare domain such as example.com, or a full URL

tools.name: list_verified_capabilities
tools.description: Lists what a domain declares agents can do (OpenAPI operations, MCP tools, A2A skills, API catalog entries), each classed by safety, which ones CrawlCheck called and confirmed, and every mismatch. Read from the latest scan on file; run scan_domain first if there is none. Use before relying on a site's declared actions. For a remote MCP endpoint's status use mcp_servers.

verified_only.description: Return only the capabilities that were confirmed

tools.name: mcp_servers
tools.description: Lists the remote MCP servers the official MCP Registry shows for a domain and what each endpoint answered to a handshake: initialized, auth_required or unreachable, tool count and tool-list drift. Use before connecting to an MCP server on that domain. For a go/no-go decision on connecting use preflight with action connect; to check your own release use mcp_precheck.

domain.description: Bare domain or host, e.g. example.com

tools.name: verify_crawler_log
tools.description: Checks raw access-log lines (up to 200) and returns, for each line that names a crawler, verified, spoofed or unverifiable, by testing the source IP against that operator's published ranges. Use on your own server logs. For crawler traffic seen at crawlcheck.io itself use telemetry; for which crawlers can reach a domain use crawler_path.

lines.description: Up to 200 raw log lines, newline separated

tools.name: corpus_state
tools.description: Returns how representative CrawlCheck's public dataset is: how many distinct domains were measured, how they split by platform, rendering, size, language and kind, and which groups are under-sampled. No input. Use before quoting dataset-wide figures. For CrawlCheck's headline numbers use public_counts; for one domain's entry use registry_lookup.

tools.name: resolve_robots
tools.description: Returns whether each named answer engine, search crawler and training crawler may fetch one path under a domain's robots file, read the way crawlers read it. It also flags crawlers whose own group cancels the rules under *. Use for a robots.txt question alone. For the full path a crawler takes use crawler_path; for a corrected file use fix_robots.

tools.name: resolve_rights
tools.description: Returns, signed, what a site declares AI may do with a page: train, ground, summarize, cite or transact. Each answer is merged from robots.txt, Content-Signal, ai.txt, TDM-Rep, robots meta, X-Robots-Tag and the terms page, with the deciding signal and any conflicts. Use for permission questions; not legal advice. For whether crawlers can actually reach the site use crawler_path.

agent.description: One crawler product token (e.g. GPTBot) to answer for that agent alone

tools.name: check_site_safety
tools.description: Returns whether a domain is listed as malware or phishing on public block lists, which list says so, and where to check it and request a review. It adds HSTS preload and hacked-site signs from the latest scan; a list not read is reported as unread, never clean. Use when the only question is danger. For a go/no-go decision use preflight.

tools.name: draft_llms
tools.description: Returns a draft llms file built from the domain's homepage and up to 25 pages it declares, using their titles and descriptions, for the owner to edit before publishing. Use when a site has no llms.txt or a weak one. For a corrected robots.txt use fix_robots; for a starter entitymap.json use fix_entitymap.

tools.name: fix_robots
tools.description: Returns the domain's served robots file corrected: rules under * copied into named groups that lacked them, a Sitemap line added when missing, or a minimal file when the server answered with HTML. Every change is listed at the top. Use to repair robots.txt. To read what the current file allows each crawler use resolve_robots.

tools.name: fix_entitymap
tools.description: Returns a starter entity map built from the domain's latest scan: business name, phone, coordinates and declared service areas, with anything the site never stated marked TODO, never guessed. Use when a site has no entitymap.json or a wrong one. Needs a scan on file; run scan_domain first if there is none. For llms.txt use draft_llms.

tools.name: video_check
tools.description: Returns a checklist on one YouTube video for search and AI visibility (metadata, chapters, captions, storyboard), each row with what it read and whether it passed or was only measured. Cached for six hours unless fresh is true. Use for one video. For a channel's upload list use video_channel; for how a website embeds its videos use video_site.

tools.name: video_channel
tools.description: Returns a YouTube channel's totals and up to 200 of its uploads (id, title, publish date) in the channel's upload-list order. Give the handle or, without one, the channel id. Use to see which videos a channel has; it runs no checks. For the checks on one video use video_check; for how a website embeds the channel's videos use video_site.

tools.name: video_site
tools.description: Returns how a website carries its videos: YouTube embeds, facades and page-builder widgets on the homepage and up to 60 sitemap pages, and its VideoObject markup with any missing required properties. Given a channel handle, also how many of that channel's videos the site carries. For one video use video_check; for a channel's uploads use video_channel.

tools.name: registry_lookup
tools.description: Returns whether a domain is in CrawlCheck's registry and which agent files it serves: the llms and agents files, a media kit, a tested entity graph, an AI access policy and agent-callable surfaces. With no domain, returns counts per shelf. Rows come from fetching llms.txt, agents.md and the rest, never from self-reports or payment. For what those surfaces actually do use list_verified_capabilities.

domain.description: A bare domain. Omit for the corpus-wide shelf counts.

shelf.description: Filter the list to one shelf: llms, agents, mediakit, entity, aipolicy, agentapi

tools.name: crawler_path
tools.description: Returns, for each crawler identity (ClaudeBot, GPTBot, Googlebot and others), where its path into a domain stops: edge, robots file, then the page, JSON-LD, sitemap, llms file and entity map. Give agent for one crawler and a one-line answer. Uses the record on file or scans first. Use for which AI crawlers can reach a site. For robots.txt rules alone use resolve_robots.

agent.description: Identity id or label, e.g. claudebot, GPTBot, Googlebot

fresh.description: Scan now instead of using the record on file

tools.name: public_counts
tools.description: Returns CrawlCheck's own figures, read from the source with a timestamp: sites measured, domains in the corpus, crawler visits over a rolling window, sections, findings and guides published. No input. Use when quoting a CrawlCheck figure about itself. For dataset coverage by group use corpus_state; for which crawlers visit CrawlCheck use telemetry.

tools.name: telemetry
tools.description: Returns verified-crawler traffic observed on CrawlCheck's own site: which named crawlers arrived, how many identity claims were confirmed against operator ranges, and how many were forged. No input. Use as live evidence of which crawlers are active. To verify crawlers in your own server logs use verify_crawler_log.

tools.name: fix_mostly_code
tools.description: Returns a fix plan for the PAGE_IS_MOSTLY_CODE finding, starting with the homepage's bytes by category. It names the largest blocks and what to do with each, orders the steps with the text ratio after each, and marks the step that clears the finding. Give domain (fetched now) or a report id. For why other findings fired use explain_finding.

id.description: Report id: plan from the stored scan instead of fetching

tools.name: fix_stale_cache
tools.description: Returns a fix plan for the STALE_CACHE_SERVED finding, read from the homepage fetched now. It gives the Age, each cache layer named in the headers in purge order, the declared HTML lifetime, a fresh-read comparison, and whether a purge clears the finding. It purges nothing. Give domain or a report id. For why other findings fired use explain_finding.

id.description: Report id; the page is still fetched now, because cache state is live

tools.name: fix_machine_chain
tools.description: Returns a fix plan for the MACHINE_CHAIN_HEAVY finding: the files a crawler reads before the page and the 404s for absent agent files. Then measured reductions, with the chain size after each step and the step that clears the finding. Give domain: measured now, or with a licence key from its latest scan; a report id needs one. For why other findings fired use explain_finding.

domain.description: The site's domain. Measured now; with a licence key for it (x-crawlcheck-key), its latest scan on file is used instead

id.description: A report id; answers only with a licence key for that report's domain

tools.name: explain_finding
tools.description: Returns why CrawlCheck decided one finding: the rule and its revision, the fetches compared, when the condition held, and proof it is inside the signed record. Give a d1: or f1: id, a domain for its top finding, or domain plus code. Use to audit or dispute a finding. Fix plans exist in fix_robots, fix_entitymap, fix_mostly_code, fix_stale_cache and fix_machine_chain.

id.description: d1: decision id, f1: finding id, or report id

domain.description: Bare domain; alone it explains the top finding

tools.name: machine_record
tools.description: Returns the stored machine record of one past scan: subject, grade, every finding, capabilities with verification, and the evidence roots, manifest and verifier links needed to check it offline. Give a report, d1:, f1: or manifest id, or a domain for its latest. It never scans. For a new scan use scan_domain; for the current signed answer use resolve_domain.

tools.name: mcp_precheck
tools.description: Returns, signed, what public change logs will record when an MCP server ships a new tool list. It lists tools added or removed, descriptions rewritten, schemas widened, annotation escalations, and whether the version moved. Use before releasing your own server: give its registry name or endpoint, the new tools and version. It calls no tool on it. To check another server use mcp_servers.

server_name.description: Name in the MCP Registry, e.g. io.github.owner/server

endpoint.description: Remote MCP endpoint URL, e.g. https://mcp.example.com/mcp

tools.description: The new tools/list tools array; omit to read the endpoint live
